audit.whatIsWrong: Seven fields attribute the projectile reflect to Mel's ULTIMATE — 'never fan W rockets while her R is up', 'bait her R or wait it out', 'catch your rockets with R', 'a well-timed R bait'.
audit.why: The reflect is Rebuttal, her W: Riot's text has her form a barrier that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her taking damage, and grants Move Speed. Golden Eclipse (R) is a global strike on Overwhelm stacks with no reflect at all. Getting the slot wrong ruins the timing the whole page is built on: Rebuttal is 38s at rank 1 falling to 26s, while the ultimate is 120s — a reader waiting out 'her R' before firing rockets waits for the wrong cooldown and eats the barrier anyway. It also matters that Rebuttal's Move Speed covers her walk out of the nest.
audit.corrected: Reflect reattributed to Rebuttal with its 38s in whys[4], whys[5], whys[6], spikes[2], spikes[3], early, mid, wants.you[2], wants.foe[1], plus tldr, winCon, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: packet defect: 'never names any of Mel's abilities'. The full layer names only Solar Snare, and no cooldown appears anywhere.
audit.why: Rebuttal's 38s at rank 1 is the longest cooldown in her kit and the one that decides whether your commit lands at all. Solar Snare is an 11s root from 1000 range, Radiant Volley 10s at 950, Golden Eclipse 120s. Three fields also call Mel 'short range' — a 950 Q against a 350 turret is not short, and the mirror already established that Micro-Rockets' 1325 is what actually wins the range war.
